q: Who was the Governor-General of India at the time of the Revolt of 1857?
exp: Lord Canning was Governor-General (1856-62) and became the first Viceroy in 1858.

q: Which pass connects Srinagar with Leh?
exp: Zoji La, in the Pir Panjal/Himalaya region, links Srinagar and Leh on NH-1.

q: The Kesaria stupa, one of the largest Buddhist stupas in the world, is located in which district of Bihar?
exp: Kesaria Stupa is in East Champaran (Purvi Champaran) district.

q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Election Commission of India?
exp: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission.

q: Which of the following is a direct tax?
exp: A direct tax is borne by the person on whom it is levied, e.g. income tax; GST and duties are indirect.

q:
Match the organisation/movement with its founder.
P. Servants of India Society   Q. Swaraj Party   R. Satyashodhak Samaj
1. G. K. Gokhale   2. C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru   3. Jyotiba Phule
exp: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society (1905), Das and Motilal Nehru the Swaraj Party (1923), Phule the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873).

q: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
exp: Gujarat has the longest mainland coastline (about 1,600 km), followed by Andhra Pradesh.

q: The river Gandak, which flows through Bihar, is also known as
exp: The Gandak is called Narayani (or Saligrami) in Nepal.

q:
Statement I: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
Statement II: The Rajya Sabha has the power to reject a Money Bill.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
exp: Money Bills originate only in the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations within 14 days and cannot reject them.

q: Which part of the human eye controls the amount of light entering it?
exp: The iris adjusts the size of the pupil and hence the amount of light entering the eye.

q: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and
exp: The Marathas were defeated by Ahmad Shah Abdali's Afghan forces in 1761.

q: The Western Ghats are also known as the
exp: In Maharashtra, the Western Ghats are called the Sahyadri range.

q: The famous Sonepur cattle fair in Bihar is held near the confluence of which two rivers?
exp: The Harihar Kshetra (Sonepur) fair is held at the Ganga-Gandak confluence in Saran district.

q: The writ of Habeas Corpus literally means
exp: Habeas Corpus is issued to produce a detained person before a court to examine legality of detention.

q: The Human Development Index (HDI) is published by which organisation?
exp: HDI, combining health, education and income indices, is published by the UN Development Programme.

q: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
exp: Mountbatten served from 15 August 1947 to June 1948, followed by C. Rajagopalachari.

q: The Jog Falls, one of the highest waterfalls of India, is formed by which river?
exp: The Sharavathi river plunges down the Western Ghats in Karnataka to form Jog Falls.

q: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was launched against which system?
exp: Gandhi's first satyagraha in India was for peasants forced to grow indigo on 3/20 of their land.

q: Who appoints the Governor of a state in India?
exp: Under Article 155, the Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.

q: India's first satellite, Aryabhata, was launched in which year?
exp: Aryabhata was launched on 19 April 1975 with Soviet help.

q: The ancient treatise on statecraft 'Arthashastra' was written by
exp: Kautilya (Chanakya), minister of Chandragupta Maurya, wrote the Arthashastra.

q: Which state is the largest producer of tea in India?
exp: Assam produces more than half of India's tea.

q: Bhikhari Thakur, known as the 'Shakespeare of Bhojpuri', is associated with which folk theatre form?
exp: Bhikhari Thakur of Saran popularised Bidesia, a theatre form on the pain of migration.

q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
exp: Under Article 89, the Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

q: The financial year in India runs from
exp: India's financial year starts on 1 April and ends on 31 March.

q: The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 from which place?
exp: The AICC passed the Quit India resolution at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay.

q: The river Brahmaputra is known by which name in Tibet?
exp: The Brahmaputra is the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh and Jamuna in Bangladesh.

q: Vikramshila Mahavihara, an ancient centre of learning in Bihar, was established by which Pala king?
exp: Dharmapala (late 8th century) founded Vikramshila near Bhagalpur.

q: How many Schedules does the Constitution of India contain at present?
exp: The Constitution has 12 Schedules (the 12th, added in 1992, lists municipal functions).

q: Which vitamin is synthesised in human skin on exposure to sunlight?
exp: UV-B rays convert 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin into vitamin D3.

q: The Jnanpith Award is given for outstanding contribution in the field of
exp: The Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honour.

q: Who is the author of the Hindi novel 'Godan'?
exp: Godan (1936) by Munshi Premchand portrays the plight of a peasant, Hori.

q: The Thomas Cup is associated with which sport?
exp: The Thomas Cup is the world men's team championship in badminton.

q: International Yoga Day is observed on
exp: The UN General Assembly declared 21 June as International Day of Yoga in 2014.

q: Which is the national flower of India?
exp: The lotus (Nelumbo nucifera) is India's national flower.

q: Which Ashokan inscription describes the Kalinga war and Ashoka's remorse?
exp: Rock Edict XIII records the bloody Kalinga war (261 BCE) and Ashoka's turn to dhamma.

q: Which of the following is NOT a Himalayan range?
exp: The Aravallis are an old fold-mountain range in Rajasthan; Himadri, Himachal and Shiwalik are Himalayan ranges.

q: The tomb of Sher Shah Suri is located at which place in Bihar?
exp: Sher Shah's tomb stands in the middle of a lake at Sasaram (Rohtas district).

q: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of
exp: The Directive Principles were inspired by the Irish Constitution.

q: Who is regarded as the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'?
exp: M. S. Swaminathan led high-yielding wheat and rice programmes; Kurien was the father of the White Revolution.
